"Nine collapses. The four class parameters became twelve (the four surveyed plus eight the surveys never looked at), and 142 sites land on ~26 shapes of which 12 declare ZERO own fields; the widest shape has 4.

(1) THE ROOT REJECTION PAIR, NOW DECLARED EXACTLY ONCE IN THE WHOLE TREE. Survey 1 proposed RejectionDetails{rejected_value, accepted_values}; survey 2 re-declared the identical pair inside CapabilityRejectionDetails; and the committed ErrorProblem (src/core/errors/details.py:120-121) had ALREADY declared it a third time. One `_RejectionFields` mixin now owns it, ErrorProblem inherits it (dropping its copies), RejectionDetails inherits it, and the root-level and per-item keys are incapable of drifting apart in name or type -- the entire premise of the pin's two-level rejection shape. This is the drift the surveys measured (3 spellings of the accepted set, 6+ of the rejected value) landing on two names, declared once.

(2) EntityRef+Problems, PROPOSED FOUR TIMES, NOW A BASE THAT IS NEVER A LEAF. Survey 1's ValidationDetails base, survey 3's ConfigurationFaultDetails, survey 4's CreativeRejectedDetails base AND the committed AdapterFailureDetails(EntityRefDetails, UpstreamCallDetails, ProblemsDetails) were one composition under four spellings. EntityProblemsDetails owns it and AdapterFailureDetails is re-based onto it. Critically it is a BASE ONLY: making it AdCPConfigurationError's parameter (the original catalog's choice) made eight validation/creative shapes assignable at a configuration raise site with mypy silent -- the hole survey 3 rejected its own option (b) for. Every family gets its own zero-field leaf instead, so each parameter still discriminates.

(3) ENTITY+PROBLEMS+REJECTION IS ONE NAME, COMPOSED FOUR WAYS. EntityRejectionDetails is declared once and reached by composition -- RejectionValidationDetails(ValidationDetails, EntityRejectionDetails), CapabilityRejectionDetails(CapabilityDetails, EntityRejectionDetails), AmbiguousMatchDetails -- and used directly as the shared parameter of AdCPGoneError / AdCPConflictError / AdCPBudgetExceededError / AdCPMediaBuyRejectedError. No shape ever restates (EntityProblemsDetails, RejectionDetails).

(4) THE REJECTION PAIR LEFT THE VALIDATION ROOT, WHICH KILLED THREE DOUBLE CHANNELS AT ONCE. With ValidationDetails carrying it, TypeMismatchDetails had `expected_types` AND an inherited `accepted_values`; TimeWindowDetails had `start_time` AND an inherited `rejected_value`; PricingValidationDetails had four money fields AND an inherited `rejected_value`. Only the ~15 sites that genuinely reject a value against a closed set now get the pair, via one leaf.

(5) ONE VALUE/BOUND VOCABULARY FOR MONEY, COUNTS AND SECONDS. The catalog previously spelled "a number against its bound" three ways: PricingValidationDetails{bid_price, floor_price, package_budget, min_spend_per_package} at media_buy_create.py:1490/1510, RangeProblem{minimum,maximum} at the mock adapter's ceilings, and rejected_value=str(budget) at google_ad_manager.py:1381. Now the value ALWAYS goes to rejected_value and the bound ALWAYS to RangeProblem -- pricing floor, min spend, impressions ceiling, budget ceiling and the current-spend floor at google_ad_manager.py:1409 use one construction. PricingValidationDetails drops from 6 own fields to 2.

(6) THE SLASH-JOINED FORMAT COMPOSITE IS GONE. media_buy_update.py:276, creatives/_assignments.py:237 and media_buy_create.py:3827 all built f"{agent_url}/{format_id}", and the original catalog moved that discarded structure INTO rejected_value/accepted_values -- relocating the f-string instead of removing it, and duplicating agent_url/format_id which EntityRefDetails already declares. One FormatRef{agent_url, format_id} now serves both the rejected side (FormatProblem.format) and the accepted set (CreativeFormatDetails.accepted_formats).

(7) ONE FIELD-POINTER GRAMMAR, ONE REFERENT. first_validation_error_field() (src/core/exceptions.py:1105) is the only producer of a field path anywhere in the catalog; the hand-rolled ".".join(err["loc"]) proposed for capability_declarations.py:272 (yielding `specialisms.0`) is deleted. ErrorProblem.field is documented as a request-payload pointer in bracket notation and nothing else, so media_buy_update.py:240's stored creative status moves to rejected_value.

(8) THE PROBLEM-LIST SYNONYMS, NOW UNIFORM ACROSS TWELVE CLASSES RATHER THAN FOUR. validation_errors / config_errors / adapter_errors / creative_errors / violations / features / requested / the eleven *_any_of keys / the computed f"unbacked_{field}" keys / rejection_reasons all reach the wire as problems[]. Two pairs that were literally one list under two key names become one construction: adapter.validate_media_buy_request() (mock_ad_server.py:668 vs media_buy_create.py:3503) and the three _validate_targeting copies (kevel.py:238, triton_digital.py:165, google_ad_manager.py:582).

(9) THE CAPABILITY-NAME CHANNEL ACTUALLY CLOSES. The original catalog claimed 11 spellings collapsed to one while leaving a 12th alive (targeting_capabilities.py:247 details={"feature": ...}, invisible because it is in the advisory Error.of lane no survey scanned) and while minting a 13th classification token ("media_type_multiple") inside the enum meant to name subjects. Covering the advisory lane and deleting that token makes the claim true, and it costs no new shape: CapabilityDetails now extends EntityProblemsDetails, so media_buy_update.py:1070 emits product_id like the other three families instead of a degenerate one-element problems list, and CapabilityProblemsDetails/CapabilityEntityDetails both disappear.

violations.where: Catalog proposals for src/core/tools/media_buy_update.py:276 (rejected_value=f"{c.agent_url}/{c.format}", accepted_values=sorted(f"{u}/{fid}" ...)); src/core/tools/creatives/_assignments.py:237 (rejected_value=creative_format_display, which is built at _assignments.py:218-224 as exactly that f-string); src/core/tools/media_buy_create.py:3827 (rejected_value=f"{creative.agent_url}/{creative.format}"). violations.what: A rejected money amount has two competing channels inside one shape family, and the catalog uses both — typed root fields (bid_price, package_budget) at some sites, the inherited rejected_value at others.

violations.what: TimeWindowDetails gives the offending instant a second spelling alongside the rejected_value it inherits, at a site that rejects exactly one value.

violations.what: One field-pointer fact gets two grammars: the canonical bracket-notation builder, and a hand-rolled dotted join. ErrorProblem.field is additionally loaded with two different referents.
violations.where: Catalog proposal for src/core/schemas/capability_declarations.py:272 — `field=".".join(str(part) for part in err["loc"])` — against src/core/exceptions.py:1187 / src/core/validation_helpers.py:54, which use the existing builder `first_validation_error_field` (src/core/exceptions.py:1107). Second referent clash: src/core/tools/media_buy_create.py:497 (problem field=f"packages[{idx}].creative_ids", a request pointer) vs src/core/tools/media_buy_update.py:240 (problem field="status", a stored creative state the buyer never sent — verified at media_buy_update.py:242, `c.status` off the DB row).
violations.why_it_breaks_a_rule: Rule 8 — one channel per fact, and `field` is a first-class fact whose grammar is already fixed. src/core/exceptions.py:1110-1114 states the rule explicitly: list indices render as `[i]` "so boundary-derived paths such as `packages[0].budget` align with the `packages[].budget` field strings raised by the implementation layer." The catalog's dotted join yields `specialisms.0`, which does not align, and duplicates a helper that already exists (CLAUDE.md DRY invariant: duplicated logic is a defect). violations.fix: Reuse the existing pointer builder for every Pydantic-loc site, including capability_declarations.py:272 (export it if the import direction is wrong — do not re-derive it). State in ErrorProblem's docstring that `field` is a request-payload pointer in bracket notation and nothing else; for an entity-state problem such as media_buy_update.py:240, carry the state in rejected_value with subject_type/subject_id and leave `field` unset, or name the request pointer that referenced the creative.

violations.what: accepted_values is populated with URL schemes — values the named field cannot hold — and absent-vs-malformed is left to be classified by whether that key is populated.
violations.where: Catalog proposal for src/adapters/gam/managers/creatives.py:732: `problems=[ErrorProblem(code=VALIDATION_ERROR, accepted_values=["http", "https"])]` with the site's existing `field="url"` (verified: the guard is `url.startswith(("http://", "https://"))`). verdicts.lens: pin-conformance vs ../adcp/dist/schemas/3.1.1/error-details/*.json + core/error.json + enums/error-code.json + enums/media-buy-valid-action.json + enums/action-not-allowed-reason.json + docs/3.1.1/building/by-layer/L3/error-handling.mdx (all read in full, not via the summaries). Clean on three hunt items: (a) no clamped shape is modelled permissively — agent-permission-denied.json and billing-not-permitted-for-agent.json are the only additionalProperties:false files and neither is in the catalog; (b) the committed VersionUnsupportedDetails correctly models the pin's one required field (supported_versions) as required and core/version-envelope.json has no required fields; (c) RejectionDetails' placement claim is accurate — core/error.json's `details` description does put rejected_value/accepted_values at the details ROOT with neither required. Everything below is a genuine divergence I could confirm against file text.

violations.what: The catalog invents a rich `details` shape for CONFIGURATION_ERROR, a code the pin explicitly leaves shapeless under a minimal-disclosure clamp — and fills it with seller deployment internals. `AdCPConfigurationError._code = ErrorCode.CONFIGURATION_ERROR` (src/core/exceptions.py:666, confirmed), and the pin is normative twice over: enums/error-code.json enumDescription for CONFIGURATION_ERROR says "The code itself is the discriminator; no `error.details` shape is defined for this code (mirroring the minimal-disclosure precedent of `AGENT_SUSPENDED` / `AGENT_BLOCKED`). Sellers SHOULD populate `error.message` with operator-actionable detail"; docs/3.1.1/building/by-layer/L3/error-handling.mdx:853 repeats it — "`CONFIGURATION_ERROR` carries no `error.details` shape (the minimal-disclosure precedent ... applies). `error.message` carries the diagnostic ... without leaking deployment internals to the buyer." The catalog does the opposite: it makes EntityProblemsDetails the type parameter for this code and routes ~19 sites through it, plus SetupIncompleteDetails, RangeProblem, DependencyProblem and TypeMismatchDetails. The payloads are exactly the internals the prose names: `ErrorProblem(rejected_value=str(advertiser_id))` publishes the seller's configured GAM advertiser id (google_ad_manager.py:157); `accepted_values=["service_account_key_file","service_account_json","refresh_token"]` publishes the seller's credential-slot inventory (google_ad_manager.py:173); RangeProblem publishes the seller's internal replay-TTL bounds (idempotency_policy.py:61,69); SetupIncompleteDetails publishes the seller's outstanding setup-task keys (media_buy_create.py:2057); DependencyProblem/ErrorProblem publish the seller's unbacked protocol and block declarations (capability_declarations.py:146,261,321). The catalog also silently REVERSES the one survey decision that was pin-correct: survey 3 proposed `NONE (details unset)` at capability_declarations.py:252, and collapse (4) overrides it to emit TypeMismatchDetails. Open question 4 further inverts the pin's own distinction — the pin separates ACCOUNT_SETUP_REQUIRED ("buyer-side onboarding incomplete") from CONFIGURATION_ERROR ("seller-side deployment incomplete"), so a tenant that has not finished ITS setup checklist is correctly CONFIGURATION_ERROR, which means SetupIncompleteDetails must not exist at all rather than being reconciled against account-setup-required.json.
violations.where: catalog `class_parameters` entry "AdCPConfigurationError (src/core/exceptions.py:653) → EntityProblemsDetails"; shapes SetupIncompleteDetails, RangeProblem, DependencyProblem, TypeMismatchDetails (serves_error_classes lists AdCPConfigurationError); sites src/adapters/google_ad_manager.py:157,173,449, src/core/idempotency_policy.py:61,69, src/core/tools/media_buy_create.py:2057, src/core/schemas/capability_declarations.py:146,252,261,272,321
violations.why_it_breaks_a_rule: Rules 1 and 2: an error class declares its shape as `AdCPError[SomeDetails]` and the EXCEPTION CLASS owns the code — so the shape a class is parameterized on is emitted under that class's code, unconditionally. Binding any details shape to a class whose code the pin declares shapeless makes rule 1's declaration itself non-conformant, and no per-site choice can undo it. It also breaks rule 3's own justification chain: the pin routes this diagnostic to `error.message`, i.e. the design's sanctioned free-text-free destination for this code is the message + internal_detail, not a declared shape.
violations.fix: Leave `AdCPConfigurationError` un-parameterized (or parameterize it on a shape that is never populated) and drop SetupIncompleteDetails, RangeProblem-for-config, DependencyProblem and the TypeMismatchDetails-at-252 mapping from the catalog. Each of the ~19 config sites keeps its first-class `field=` (which the surveys correctly add) and moves its diagnostic to `internal_detail` / the operator-facing `error.message`, per error-handling.mdx:853. If any of those facts is judged genuinely buyer-actionable, that is a protocol-behavior change and needs the CLAUDE.md spec-grounding gate — spec section + storyboard step cited before code — not an entry in this catalog.

violations.what: `ProblemsDetails.problems` / `ErrorProblem` is used as the multi-item validation channel where the pin canonicalizes `issues[]`, and the migration drops a pinned REQUIRED field of that structure. core/error.json declares a top-level `issues` array whose items require `pointer` (RFC 6901), `message` AND `keyword` ("Schema keyword that rejected the payload ... so agents can pattern-match on rejection class without parsing message text"), describes its "Primary use" as VALIDATION_ERROR multi-field rejections, and states the ONLY sanctioned `details` spelling for it: "Sellers MAY mirror `issues[]` here as `details.issues` for backward compatibility ... new consumers SHOULD prefer the top-level `issues` field." error-handling.mdx:136-139 repeats it and adds a MUST: when `issues` is present, `field` MUST be set from `issues[0].pointer` translated to JSONPath-lite. `grep -rn "issues" src/` returns nothing outside unrelated prose — the channel is unimplemented — and the catalog routes precisely the schema-validation sites into `details.problems`, a seller-specific key, while survey 1 records the loss verbatim: "ErrorProblem has no slot for the pin's issues[].keyword". This is the same class of defect the catalog itself indicts (five spellings of one list) applied one level up: `problems` is a sixth spelling of a concept the pin already named.
violations.where: catalog shapes ValidationDetails / EntityProblemsDetails (via committed ProblemsDetails, src/core/errors/details.py:219) applied at src/core/exceptions.py:1187, src/core/validation_helpers.py:54, src/core/schemas/capability_declarations.py:272
violations.why_it_breaks_a_rule: Rule 4: the canonical-key rule the catalog invokes for `rejected_value`/`accepted_values` comes from the same `details` description that canonicalizes this list as `issues` (and `details.issues` when mirrored). Applying rule 4 to one pair of keys from that paragraph while substituting a seller-specific name for the structure named in the paragraph above it is selective grounding, and rule 3's "classification uses `code`" cannot excuse discarding `keyword`, which classifies the SCHEMA rejection, not the error.
violations.fix: For the schema-validation sites, emit the pinned channel: populate top-level `issues[]` with `pointer` (RFC 6901), `message`, `keyword` from the Pydantic error's `type`, and set the exception's `field` from `issues[0].pointer` translated to JSONPath-lite per the MUST. Either add `issues` as a first-class AdCPError field (then rule 8 forbids duplicating it into any shape) or, at minimum, name the details key `issues` rather than `problems` and carry `pointer`/`keyword` on the item. Do not land these three sites on `problems` while the pinned channel is unimplemented.

violations.where: catalog proposed_kwargs at src/core/schemas/capability_declarations.py:272 (`field=".".join(str(part) for part in err["loc"])`) vs src/core/exceptions.py:1187 / src/core/validation_helpers.py:54 (`field=jsonpath_lite(e["loc"])`)
violations.what: Two pointer formats for one channel, one of them conformant to neither pinned format. The pin defines exactly two spellings for a field path: JSONPath-lite on `error.field` ("e.g., 'packages[0].targeting'", core/error.json) and RFC 6901 on `issues[].pointer` ("e.g., '/packages/0/targeting/geo_countries/2'"), with an explicit note that the two differ and MUST be translated when crossed. A dot-joined Pydantic `loc` yields `packages.0.targeting` — neither. The catalog's own headline claims these Pydantic sites "collapse to one construction"; they do not.
violations.why_it_breaks_a_rule: Rule 4: `ErrorProblem.field` is a pinned-vocabulary slot, and a field renamed or reformatted away from the pin's spelling is exactly what the declared-class migration exists to stop. It also breaks the catalog's own DRY claim (CLAUDE.md DRY invariant) by shipping two builders for one fact.
violations.fix: Use one helper for every Pydantic `loc` → path conversion, emitting RFC 6901 on `issues[].pointer` and JSONPath-lite on `field`, and delete the dot-join at capability_declarations.py:272.

violations.what: `ActionRequestDetails.attempted_action` adopts a pinned key name with a value domain that has ZERO intersection with the pinned enum, and types it `str` where the pin types it as a closed enum ref. error-details/action-not-allowed.json declares `attempted_action` as `$ref: /schemas/3.1.1/enums/media-buy-valid-action.json`, and required alongside `reason`. That enum's members are `pause`, `resume`, `cancel`, `extend_flight`, `increase_budget`, `update_creative_assignments`, … I read src/adapters/constants.py:6-17: UPDATE_ACTIONS keys are `pause_media_buy`, `resume_media_buy`, `pause_package`, `resume_package`, `update_package_budget`, `update_package_impressions`, `activate_order`, `submit_for_approval`, `approve_order`, `archive_order` — not one of which is a member. The same seller-internal vocabulary is then poured into the PIN'S OWN canonical keys: `rejected_value=action` and `accepted_values=sorted(REQUIRED_UPDATE_ACTIONS)` at src/adapters/constants.py:42 and google_ad_manager.py:1599. A buyer classifier keyed on `details.attempted_action` (documented as a media-buy-valid-action value) reads `pause_package` and fails to match; `accepted_values` is defined by the pin as "the closed set the seller would have accepted at this field", and the pinned closed set for an update action is that enum. The catalog knows this — open question 2 states the tokens "do not intersect the pinned vocabulary" — and demotes it to an open question while still shipping the field name and the kwargs.
violations.where: catalog shape ActionRequestDetails (`attempted_action: str | None`), applied at src/adapters/broadstreet/adapter.py:704 and src/adapters/google_ad_manager.py:1474; CapabilityRejectionDetails kwargs at src/adapters/constants.py:42 and src/adapters/google_ad_manager.py:1599
violations.why_it_breaks_a_rule: Rule 4: when a key is the pin's, the pin's spelling AND its declared type come together — adopting `attempted_action` while widening it from a pinned enum ref to free `str` is a rename in the one direction the rule cannot detect, and putting non-enum tokens into `rejected_value`/`accepted_values` is precisely 'a canonical key filled by a seller-specific variant'. Rule 3 is also mis-applied in the catalog's stated justification: the pin's `reason` is a CLOSED registered enum (enums/action-not-allowed-reason.json: wrong_status, not_supported_on_product, not_supported_on_buy, mode_mismatch), not the free text the rule bars.
violations.fix: Either (a) rename the field off the pin — e.g. `attempted_update_action` — so the pinned key is not claimed by a non-pinned vocabulary, and leave `rejected_value`/`accepted_values` unset at constants.py:42 / google_ad_manager.py:1599 until the tokens are translated; or (b) translate UPDATE_ACTIONS keys to media-buy-valid-action members at the boundary, type `attempted_action` with that enum, and take the translation through the spec-grounding gate. Resolve before the shape lands; do not ship the pinned key name over an untranslated vocabulary.

violations.what: A pinned shape's canonical key is replaced by a seller-specific variant for the very condition the pin names. error-details/budget-too-low.json declares `minimum_budget` ("Seller's minimum budget for this product") + `currency` ("ISO 4217 currency code"), and enums/error-code.json describes BUDGET_TOO_LOW as "Budget is below the seller's minimum." I read src/core/tools/media_buy_create.py:1504-1517: the guard is `package_budget < selected_option.min_spend_per_package` — verbatim that condition — yet the catalog preserves the seller key `min_spend_per_package` as a declared field on PricingValidationDetails while spelling its sibling `currency` the pin's way, so half the pinned pair is adopted and half is not. The same fact is spelled a third way as `RangeProblem.minimum` for the mock adapter's budget floor. `AdCPBudgetTooLowError` with `_code = ErrorCode.BUDGET_TOO_LOW` already exists (src/core/exceptions.py:861-865) and is already raised (media_buy_create.py:2179), so the pinned code and class are both available and the catalog neither uses them here nor flags the mismatch anywhere in its six collapses or six open questions.
violations.where: catalog shape PricingValidationDetails field `min_spend_per_package: Decimal | None` applied at src/core/tools/media_buy_create.py:1510; RangeProblem applied at src/adapters/mock_ad_server.py:668 and src/core/tools/media_buy_create.py:3503 for the budget ceiling/floor
violations.why_it_breaks_a_rule: Rule 4: `minimum_budget`/`currency` is the pinned spelling for 'the seller's minimum budget and its denomination', and `min_spend_per_package` / `minimum` are seller-specific variants of it — the exact drift the epic removes. Rule 2 compounds it: because the shape names no code, only the exception class can put this on the pin's footing, and the catalog leaves it on AdCPValidationError.
violations.fix: Rename the field to the pin's `minimum_budget` and reuse the already-declared `currency`; then decide, through the spec-grounding gate, whether media_buy_create.py:1510 and the mock adapter's budget floor should raise `AdCPBudgetTooLowError` (BUDGET_TOO_LOW) rather than VALIDATION_ERROR, and record the citation. Do not carry three spellings of one bound into the migration.

violations.what: CreativeRejectedDetails — and with it the wire code CREATIVE_REJECTED — is bound to three sites whose condition the pin governs with a MUST on a different code. enums/error-code.json, CREATIVE_NOT_FOUND: "Referenced creative does not exist in the agent's creative library. … Sellers MUST return this code uniformly for any creative_id not owned by the calling account — never distinguish 'exists in another tenant' from 'does not exist', which would enable cross-tenant enumeration." I confirmed `AdCPCreativeRejectedError._code = ErrorCode.CREATIVE_REJECTED` (src/core/exceptions.py:936) and that a correctly-coded class already exists — `_code = ErrorCode.CREATIVE_NOT_FOUND` at src/core/exceptions.py:814. The three sites are exactly the not-owned case (they resolve `missing_ids` under the caller's principal) and already carry `# FIXME(#1598)` comments admitting the tension (media_buy_update.py:229, media_buy_create.py:382, :3767). The catalog keeps them on the rejected class, buries CREATIVE_NOT_FOUND in `problems[].code`, and — because the shape it binds is the mirror of error-details/creative-rejected.json — drags `policy_id`/`policy_url` ("Identifier for the violated policy") onto a lookup miss. A buyer reading `error.code` gets CREATIVE_REJECTED for a creative that simply is not theirs, which is the shape the pin's MUST closes.
violations.where: catalog `class_parameters` entry "AdCPCreativeRejectedError (src/core/exceptions.py:932) → CreativeRejectedDetails" applied at src/core/tools/media_buy_update.py:232, src/core/tools/media_buy_create.py:386 and :3770 (catalog open question 6)
violations.why_it_breaks_a_rule: Rule 2: a detail shape names no code, so the exception class is the SOLE authority on what code these sites emit — which means the class binding must be pin-correct before any shape is attached to it, and `problems[].code` cannot repair a wrong `error.code`. Leaving it as an open question is not available under rule 2's division of authority.

violations.what: CreativeRejectedDetails is filed as a pinned shape but does not mirror its pinned file field-for-field, and substitutes a non-pinned key for the pinned one. The catalog gives it `pinned_source: creative-rejected.json`, which places it under the contract stated in src/core/errors/details.py's own pinned-shapes header: "Each mirrors its file under the pinned schema bundle at dist/schemas/3.1.1/error-details/, field for field, plus any extra the pin permits and a call site actually needs." The file declares three properties — `policy_id`, `policy_url`, `reasons` (array of string, "Specific reasons the creative was rejected") — with `additionalProperties: true` and nothing required. The catalog declares two and emits `problems` in place of the third. Nothing here is schema-INVALID (reasons is optional, extras are permitted), but a buyer reading only the pinned key gets an empty rejection, and the catalog's own text concedes this needs "an explicit owner decision" (open question 5) while the shape ships as pin-mirroring regardless.
violations.where: catalog shape CreativeRejectedDetails, `pinned_source: ../adcp/dist/schemas/3.1.1/error-details/creative-rejected.json`; contract asserted at src/core/errors/details.py:126-131
